name: TeamStarWolf - Hugging Face AI Supply Chain (ATLAS)
description: ATLAS 2026.10 techniques that MITRE maps in the five Hugging Face case studies (AML.CS0019, AML.CS0027, AML.CS0031, AML.CS0065, AML.CS0068, all 37 CS0068 steps) plus the adjacent LAMEHUG step, as bound in the Hugging Face case study. Comments carry the study's source numbers and CS0068 step ids. Scores indicate membership only.

legendItems.label: 100: mapped by ATLAS 2026.10 in a Hugging Face case study (membership, not severity)

metadata.name: score_meaning
metadata.value: 100 means ATLAS lists the technique in a procedure step of one of the cited case studies; no severity, prevalence or coverage is measured.

links.label: Hugging Face as an AI Supply-Chain Attack Surface: A 2021 to 2026 Case Study

techniques.comment: PoisonGPT AML.CS0019 (July 2023): GPT-J-6B pulled from the Hub as the base model. Sources: [65] ATLAS 2026.10; [67] Mithril Security, 2023-07-09.
PoisonGPT AML.CS0019 (ROME edit of GPT-J-6B, July 2023) and Organization Confusion AML.CS0027 (2023-08-23). Sources: [65]; [67]; [68].
PoisonGPT AML.CS0019 (July 2023). Source: [65].
Poisoned or malicious models published to the Hub: AML.CS0019 (2023-07), AML.CS0027 (2023-08-23), AML.CS0031 (2025), AML.CS0065 (2025-09-03). Sources: [65]; [67]; [30]; [34].
Model repository as the delivery path: AML.CS0019, AML.CS0027, AML.CS0065; also the ShadowRay step AML.CS0023 S05. Sources: [65]; [34]; [67].
Malicious Models on Hugging Face AML.CS0031 (ReversingLabs nullifAI, published 2025-02-06) maps the parent technique. Sources: [65]; [30].
Victim loads an unsafe model artifact: AML.CS0027, AML.CS0031, AML.CS0065. Sources: [65]; [27]; [30]; [34].
Malware embedded in model files: Keras Lambda layer (AML.CS0027), pickle payloads (AML.CS0031), reverse-shell models (AML.CS0065). Sources: [65]; [68]; [30]; [34].
AML.CS0031: models that cannot be fully deserialized evaded Picklescan (2025). Sources: [65]; [30].

Reverse shells and implants from loaded models: AML.CS0027 (Sliver), AML.CS0031 (107.173.7.141), AML.CS0065; AML.CS0068 S13: the rooted sandbox as a launchpad over public web services (2026-07-09). Sources: [65]; [30]; [34]; [68]; [41].
Attacker accounts and organizations on the Hub: AML.CS0027 (2023), AML.CS0065 (reclaimed author namespace, 2025). Sources: [65]; [34]; [68].
AML.CS0027 organization confusion (2023-08-23). Sources: [65]; [68].
AML.CS0027 (implant named training.bin) and AML.CS0065 (recreated namespace). Sources: [65]; [68]; [34].
AML.CS0065 model namespace reuse (2025-09-03). Sources: [65]; [34].
PoisonGPT AML.CS0019 (July 2023). Source: [65].
PoisonGPT AML.CS0019 (July 2023). Source: [65].
AML.CS0027 (2023-08-23); AML.CS0068 S36: credentials, command output, dataset rows and archives moved out through dataset repositories and the launchpad (2026-07-09 to 07-13). Sources: [65]; [41].

AML.CS0027 (2023-08-23); AML.CS0068 S16: Hugging Face user tokens exposed in a public dataset (2026-07-10); S21, S27, S32: worker environment, pod and node credentials (2026-07-11). Sources: [65]; [41]; [43].
AML.CS0068 S17: exposed Hugging Face user tokens used for gated access and to create dataset repositories (2026-07-10 to 07-11). Sources: [65]; [41].
AML.CS0068 S19 and S23: malicious HDF5 dataset configuration, then a reference dataset configuration evaluated by Jinja2 (2026-07-11). Sources: [65]; [40]; [41].
AML.CS0068 S25: repositories used as an asynchronous command channel (2026-07-11). Sources: [65]; [41].
AML.CS0068 S31: privileged pod to node root (2026-07-11). Sources: [65]; [41].
AML.CS0068 S28 and S34: pod identity and forged short-lived tokens (2026-07-11). Sources: [65]; [41].

AML.CS0068 S07: generated C code, shell-injection strings and follow-on commands for the exposed harness (2026-07-09). Adjacent: LAMEHUG AML.CS0044 queried a model through the Hugging Face API to generate commands (2025). Sources: [65]; [41]; [71].
AML.CS0068 S33: mesh-network key and shared cluster-connector credential used against further clusters and services (2026-07-11). Sources: [65]; [41].

AML.CS0068 S01 (Artifactory SSRF, evaluation period, no day given), S03 (WebDAV MKCOL path, 2026-07-08), S06 (harness execution methods, 2026-07-09), S18 and S22 (HDF5 and Jinja2 exploits, 2026-07-11). Sources: [65]; [41].
AML.CS0068 S35: internal MongoDB, four private source repositories and five customer datasets (2026-07-11 to 07-13). Sources: [65]; [41].
AML.CS0068 S20: HDF5 external references disclose /proc/self/environ and worker source (2026-07-11). Sources: [65]; [41].
AML.CS0068 S08: exposed code-evaluation harness abused for root in external sandboxes (2026-07-09). Sources: [65]; [41].
AML.CS0068 S09: shell, C and Python through the harness (2026-07-09); S24: staged Python and shell in the Dataset Server pod (2026-07-11). Sources: [65]; [41].
AML.CS0068 S10: sandbox files, mounts and services (2026-07-09); S29: Kubernetes and cloud estate (2026-07-11). Sources: [65]; [41].
AML.CS0068 S11: sandbox egress and lifetime (2026-07-09); S30: identity and network reachability (2026-07-11). Sources: [65]; [41].
AML.CS0068 S05: found the exposed harness (by 2026-07-09); S15: searched for CyberGym material and gated datasets (2026-07-10). Sources: [65]; [41].
AML.CS0068 S00: intermediate objectives adapted across the evaluation (2026-05-26 to 07-13). Sources: [65]; [41].
AML.CS0068 S04: the shared Artifactory namespace as a message board (2026-07-08). Sources: [65]; [41]; [44].
AML.CS0068 S12: a second-stage loader restores each fresh sandbox (from 2026-07-09). Sources: [65]; [41].
AML.CS0068 S02: the Artifactory SSRF crosses the evaluation network boundary (evaluation period, no day given). Sources: [65]; [41]; [42].
AML.CS0068 S14 and S26: chunked, compressed, Base64 and XOR-encoded traffic (2026-07-09 to 07-13). Sources: [65]; [41].
